examples.en: I wrote a list of things to buy today.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 챙길 물건 목록을 만들었어요.
examples.en: I made a list of things to pack for the trip.

examples.ko: 이 목록에 이름이 없는 사람은 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: People whose names are not on this list can't go in.

examples.ko: 책 목록을 보고 읽고 싶은 책을 골랐어요.
examples.en: I looked at the book list and chose a book I want to read.

examples.ko: 손님 목록에 제 이름이 있어요? — 네, 맨 위에 있어요.
examples.en: Is my name on the guest list? — Yes, it's right at the top.

explain: 대화에서는 ‘리스트’도 많이 써요. 문서나 메뉴에는 ‘목록’이라고 써요.
explain_en: In conversation, 리스트 is also very common. In documents and menus, 목록 is what you will see written.

examples.en: I wrote the wedding date on the calendar.
I hung the new year's calendar on the wall.

examples.ko: 달력에 동그라미를 그려서 시험 날짜를 표시했어요.
examples.en: I circled the exam date on the calendar.

examples.ko: 집에 달력이 없어서 휴대폰으로 날짜를 봐요.
examples.en: There's no calendar at home, so I check the date on my phone.
I put my friend's birthday in my phone calendar.

explain: 한국 달력에는 음력 날짜가 작게 같이 적혀 있는 경우가 많아요.

dict_examples.ko: 문득 계절에 생각이 미치어 달력을 보았더니 벌써 십이월도 중순으로 접어들고 있었다.
dict_examples.en: When I suddenly thought of the season and looked at the calendar, it was already mid-December.

examples.en: I was invited to a friend's wedding.

examples.ko: 친구들한테 생일 파티 초대 문자를 보냈어요.
examples.en: I sent my friends a text inviting them to my birthday party.
Thank you for the invitation. — Thank you for coming.

examples.ko: 회사 파티 초대를 받았는데 뭘 입어야 해요?
examples.en: I got invited to a company party. What should I wear?
I went to dinner at my friend's invitation.

explain: 회사나 공식 행사에서는 ‘초청’이라는 말도 써요. 친구나 가족과는 ‘초대’를 많이 써요.

dict_examples.ko: 영화가 제작되었을 때, 나는 초대를 받아 그 시사를 보러 갔다.
dict_examples.en: When the film was made, I was invited and went to see the preview.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: In companies and official events, 초청 is also used. With friends and family, 초대 is the usual word.

examples.en: I got a wedding invitation.
I sent birthday party invitations to my friends.
I wrote the place and time on the invitation.
I sent a mobile invitation by text message.

examples.ko: 초대장 받았어요? — 아니요, 아직 못 받았어요.
examples.en: Did you get the invitation? — No, I haven't received it yet.

explain: 초대장은 종이로도 보내고, 카카오톡 같은 휴대폰 메시지로도 보내요.

Train tickets for Chuseok are already sold out.

I lost my train ticket, so I bought another at the station.

examples.en: Your train ticket has a seat number. Please sit in that seat.

The ticket office of the theater is on the first floor.

examples.en: I bought two tickets at the ticket office and went inside.
Where is the ticket office? — It's to the left of the entrance.

It was my first day at work, so I was really nervous.

examples.ko: 수업 첫날에 새 친구를 많이 만났어요.
examples.en: On the first day of class I met many new friends.
The first day was hard, but now it's fine.

examples.en: What did you do on the first day of your Korea trip? — I walked around near the hotel.

explain: ‘첫’ 뒤의 말은 보통 붙여 써요: 첫날, 첫눈, 첫사랑.
explain_en: Words after 첫 are usually written without a space: 첫날, 첫눈 (first snow), 첫사랑 (first love).

examples.ko: 결혼식 참석 여부를 내일까지 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please let me know by tomorrow whether you will attend the wedding.

examples.ko: 회의 참석 명단에 제 이름이 없어요.
examples.en: My name is not on the meeting attendance list.
I'm sorry, but it's hard for me to attend today's meeting.

examples.ko: 참석 인원이 몇 명이에요? — 열두 명이에요.
examples.en: How many people are attending? — Twelve.

examples.ko: 행사 참석은 자유예요. 시간이 있으면 오세요.
examples.en: Attending the event is up to you. Come if you have time.

en: this day, that day (the day just mentioned)

examples.en: December 12th is a Saturday. That's the day my sister gets married.

examples.ko: 다음 주 금요일은 회식이에요. 이날은 일찍 끝나요.
examples.en: Next Friday is our team dinner. We finish early that day.

examples.ko: 십 일은 제 생일이에요. 이날 친구들하고 저녁을 먹을 거예요.
examples.en: The tenth is my birthday. I'll have dinner with my friends that day.

examples.ko: 시월 구 일은 한글날이에요. 이날은 학교와 회사가 쉬어요.
examples.en: October 9 is Hangul Day. On this day, schools and companies are closed.

examples.ko: 시험은 다음 주 월요일이에요. 이날까지 열심히 공부할 거예요.
examples.en: The exam is next Monday. I'll study hard until then.

explain: 방금 말한 날을 가리켜요. 지난 일을 이야기할 때는 ‘그날’을 더 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 이날 이때까지 그런 말은 처음 들어요.
phrases.en: until this very day, in all one's life so far
phrases.nuance_en: used when something has never happened to you in your whole life until now
phrases.en_equiv: until this very day, in all one's life so far

dict_examples.ko: 망종이 4월에 들면 보리농사가 나쁘고 이날 비가 와도 농사가 잘 안된다고 한다.
dict_examples.en: They say that if Mangjong falls in April, the barley harvest is bad, and if it rains on this day, farming also goes poorly.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: Snowy Christmas Eve. We met for the first time on this day.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: It points back to the day you just mentioned. When talking about the past, 그날 is more common.

examples.en: I go to church every Sunday.
I sang at church on Christmas.
There is an old church in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 교회에서 친구를 만나서 같이 점심을 먹었어요.
examples.en: I met a friend at church and we had lunch together.

examples.ko: 교회가 어디에 있어요? — 시장 옆에 있어요.
examples.en: Where is the church? — It's next to the market.

explain_en: A Protestant church is a 교회; a Catholic church is called a 성당.

examples.ko: 결혼식에 올 손님 수는 백 명이에요.
examples.en: The number of guests coming to the wedding is 100.
The number of students has dropped a lot lately.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 오늘은 관광객 수가 적어요.
examples.en: It's raining, so there are few tourists today.

examples.ko: 교실에 있는 의자 수를 적어 봤어요.
examples.en: I wrote down the number of chairs in the classroom.

examples.ko: 회원 수가 몇 명이에요? — 이백 명쯤 돼요.
examples.en: How many members are there? — About two hundred.

explain: 모두 몇인지 말할 때 ‘수’를 써요: 학생 수, 손님 수. 0, 1, 2 같은 글자는 ‘숫자’라고 해요.
explain_en: Use 수 for how many there are in total: 학생 수, 손님 수. The written figures 0, 1, 2 are called 숫자.
